nodes.label: Synthetic geometry
nodes.title: Study of geometry using logical reasoning and constructions without coordinates or algebra.

nodes.label: Compass-and-straightedge constructions
nodes.title: Procedures for creating geometric figures using only a compass and a straightedge.

nodes.label: Drawing a circle of given radius
nodes.title: Using a compass to construct a circle with a specified radius length.

nodes.label: Use of a straightedge
nodes.title: Drawing straight lines and extending segments without measurement marks.

nodes.label: Use of a compass
nodes.title: Drawing circles/arcs and transferring distances in constructions.

nodes.label: Use of a ruler
nodes.title: Measuring and drawing line segments to scale when precision is required.

nodes.label: Use of a protractor
nodes.title: Measuring and constructing angles to specified sizes.

nodes.label: Use of a set square
nodes.title: Drawing right angles and common fixed angles (e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°) accurately.

nodes.label: Dynamic geometry software
nodes.title: Using interactive software to construct, manipulate, and explore geometric figures and invariants.

nodes.label: Precision in geometric constructions
nodes.title: Ensuring accuracy and correctness when performing constructions and measurements.

nodes.label: Real-life applications of geometric constructions
nodes.title: Applying construction techniques to practical contexts such as design, engineering, and drafting.

nodes.label: Revisiting standard geometric constructions (4, 5, 10, 13, 15)
nodes.title: Reviewing specified curriculum-numbered constructions and applying them in real-life contexts.

nodes.label: Cartesian coordinate plane
nodes.title: A two-dimensional plane with perpendicular x- and y-axes used to locate points by ordered pairs.

nodes.label: Ordered pairs (x, y)
nodes.title: Pairs of numbers that specify the position of a point on the Cartesian plane.

nodes.label: Plotting points on the plane
nodes.title: Placing points at the coordinates (x, y) on the Cartesian plane.

nodes.label: Linear relationship in context
nodes.title: A relationship between two quantities with a constant rate of change modeled by a linear equation in real-life situations.

nodes.label: Table of values for a linear relationship
nodes.title: Representing a linear relationship with paired x- and y-values to show a constant rate of change.

nodes.label: Graph of a linear function
nodes.title: A straight-line graph showing how one variable changes with another at a constant rate.

nodes.label: Slope as rate of change
nodes.title: Interpreting slope as the constant change in y for a unit change in x, often with contextual units.

nodes.label: Slope from a table
nodes.title: Computing slope using differences Δy/Δx from tabular data.

nodes.label: Slope from a graph
nodes.title: Determining slope using rise over run between two points on a line.

nodes.label: Slope formula
nodes.title: Using m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) to compute the slope between two points.

nodes.label: Start value (y-intercept)
nodes.title: The value of y when x = 0 in a linear model; represents the initial amount in context.

nodes.label: Slope-intercept form
nodes.title: Writing a linear equation as y = mx + b, identifying slope m and y-intercept b.

nodes.label: Comparing linear relationships
nodes.title: Analyzing and contrasting linear models using slope (rate of change) and intercept (start value).

nodes.label: Point of intersection of two lines
nodes.title: The coordinate pair that satisfies both linear relationships; represents where the lines meet.

nodes.label: Solving systems graphically
nodes.title: Finding the intersection point of two linear graphs to solve a system of equations.

nodes.label: Interpreting intersection in context
nodes.title: Explaining the real-world meaning of the solution to two linear relationships.

nodes.label: Selecting solution strategies (graphic, numeric, mental)
nodes.title: Choosing appropriate graphing, tabular/numeric, or mental reasoning approaches to solve linear problems.

nodes.label: Constructing linear models from context
nodes.title: Translating a real-life description into a linear equation and identifying slope and intercept.

nodes.label: Right-angled triangle
nodes.title: A triangle with one 90° angle; foundation for right-triangle geometry and trigonometry.

nodes.label: Hypotenuse of a right triangle
nodes.title: The side opposite the right angle; the longest side of a right triangle.

nodes.label: Opposite and adjacent sides relative to an angle
nodes.title: Naming the legs of a right triangle with respect to a given acute reference angle.

nodes.label: Pythagorean theorem
nodes.title: In a right triangle, a^2 + b^2 = c^2, relating legs and hypotenuse.

nodes.label: Solving for an unknown side using the Pythagorean theorem
nodes.title: Calculate a missing leg or hypotenuse when two side lengths are known.

nodes.label: Heights and distances problems
nodes.title: Word problems that model vertical heights and horizontal distances using right triangles.

nodes.label: Trigonometric ratios (right triangle)
nodes.title: Definitions of sine, cosine, and tangent as ratios of side lengths in a right triangle.

nodes.label: Sine ratio (SOH)
nodes.title: For an acute angle in a right triangle, sin(θ) = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

nodes.label: Cosine ratio (CAH)
nodes.title: For an acute angle in a right triangle, cos(θ) = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse.

nodes.label: Tangent ratio (TOA)
nodes.title: For an acute angle in a right triangle, tan(θ) = opposite ÷ adjacent.

nodes.label: Solving right triangles with trigonometric ratios
nodes.title: Use sine, cosine, or tangent with a given angle and side to find unknown sides.

nodes.label: Finding angles using inverse trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Use arcsin, arccos, or arctan to determine an angle from side-length ratios.

nodes.label: Angle of elevation
nodes.title: Angle measured upward from a horizontal line to a line of sight; common in height applications.

nodes.label: Angle of depression
nodes.title: Angle measured downward from a horizontal line to a line of sight; common in distance applications.

nodes.label: Modeling real-world situations with right triangles
nodes.title: Translate a context into a diagram, identify the reference angle and sides, and choose an appropriate theorem or ratio.

nodes.label: Translation (geometric transformation)
nodes.title: A rigid motion that slides every point by the same vector, preserving shape and size.

nodes.label: Central symmetry (point reflection)
nodes.title: A 180-degree rotation about a fixed center mapping each point to an opposite point through the center.

nodes.label: Axial symmetry (line reflection)
nodes.title: Reflection of points across a line (axis of symmetry) producing mirror images.

nodes.label: Rotation (geometric transformation)
nodes.title: A rigid motion turning points about a center by a given angle and direction, preserving distances.

nodes.label: Axis of symmetry (line of symmetry)
nodes.title: A line that divides a figure into two mirror-image halves under reflection.

nodes.label: Locating axes of symmetry in simple shapes
nodes.title: Identifying the lines that reflect a simple shape onto itself.

nodes.label: Recognising images under translation
nodes.title: Determining the image of a point or object after a given slide (vector shift).

nodes.label: Recognising images under central symmetry
nodes.title: Identifying the point-reflected image with respect to a specified center.

nodes.label: Recognising images under axial symmetry
nodes.title: Identifying the mirror image of a point or object across a given line.

nodes.label: Recognising images under rotation
nodes.title: Determining the rotated image about a center by a specified angle and direction.

nodes.label: Enlargement (dilation)
nodes.title: A transformation that scales distances from a fixed center by a scale factor k, preserving angles.

nodes.label: Centre of enlargement
nodes.title: The fixed point from which all points are scaled during an enlargement.

nodes.label: Scale factor k
nodes.title: The multiplicative factor by which lengths are scaled in an enlargement.

nodes.label: Reduction (0 < k < 1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor between 0 and 1 that decreases all lengths proportionally.

nodes.label: Magnification (k > 1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor greater than 1 that increases all lengths proportionally.

nodes.label: Rational scale factor (k ∈ Q)
nodes.title: Using a rational number as the scale factor in an enlargement.

nodes.label: Effect of enlargement on area (k^2 rule)
nodes.title: Under enlargement by scale factor k, areas are multiplied by k squared.

nodes.label: Solving problems involving enlargements
nodes.title: Applying center and scale factor to find images, missing lengths, and area changes.

nodes.label: Similarity of figures under enlargement
nodes.title: Understanding that enlargement produces similar figures with equal angles and proportional sides.

nodes.label: Image and preimage (transformations)
nodes.title: Terminology for the original figure (preimage) and its result after a transformation (image).

nodes.label: Geometric constructions 16–21 (post-primary)
nodes.title: Curriculum-specified set of standard compass-and-straightedge constructions numbered 16–21.

nodes.label: Geometric construction 22 (post-primary)
nodes.title: A specific syllabus construction task labeled as number 22.

nodes.label: Theorem (mathematics)
nodes.title: A mathematical statement that has been proven true based on axioms and prior results.

nodes.label: Proof (mathematics)
nodes.title: A logical argument establishing the truth of a theorem from axioms and previously proven results.

nodes.label: Axiom (postulate)
nodes.title: A foundational assumption accepted without proof, used to deduce theorems.

nodes.label: Corollary
nodes.title: A proposition that follows readily from a previously proven theorem.

nodes.label: Converse (of a statement)
nodes.title: A statement formed by reversing the hypothesis and conclusion of a conditional statement.

nodes.label: Logical implication (implies)
nodes.title: The logical relationship where one statement guarantees the truth of another.

nodes.label: Logical equivalence (is equivalent to)
nodes.title: Two statements that are true or false together in all cases.

nodes.label: Biconditional (if and only if)
nodes.title: A statement asserting both implication directions between two statements.

nodes.label: Proof by contradiction
nodes.title: A proof technique that assumes the negation of the desired conclusion and derives a contradiction.

nodes.label: Ratios in Euclidean geometry
nodes.title: Comparison of segment lengths and proportional relationships in geometric figures.

nodes.label: Geometric ratio theorems (post-primary)
nodes.title: Curriculum-specified theorems about ratios (e.g., numbered 11, 12, 13) used to justify proportional relations in geometry.

nodes.label: Applying theorems to solve geometric problems
nodes.title: Using established theorems and corollaries to deduce unknown measures or prove properties in geometry.

nodes.label: Deductive reasoning in geometry
nodes.title: Deriving geometric conclusions from axioms, definitions, and previously proven results.

nodes.label: Slope of a Line
nodes.title: Rate of change of y with respect to x; for two points (x1,y1) and (x2,y2), slope m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).

nodes.label: Parallel Lines via Slopes
nodes.title: Two non-coincident lines are parallel if and only if they have equal slopes (m1 = m2).

nodes.label: Perpendicular Lines via Slopes
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if their slopes are negative reciprocals (m1 * m2 = -1).

nodes.label: Standard Form of a Linear Equation (ax + by + c = 0)
nodes.title: Represents a straight line in the plane; slope is -a/b when b ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Problems Involving Slopes of Lines
nodes.title: Applying slope to determine direction, relative position (parallelism, perpendicularity), and to solve contextual problems.

nodes.label: Perpendicular Distance from a Point to a Line
nodes.title: Shortest distance from (x0,y0) to ax + by + c = 0 is d = |a x0 + b y0 + c| / sqrt(a^2 + b^2).

nodes.label: Angle Between Two Lines
nodes.title: If lines have slopes m1 and m2, then tan(theta) = |(m2 - m1) / (1 + m1 m2)| gives the acute angle between them.

nodes.label: Internal Division of a Line Segment (Section Formula)
nodes.title: Point dividing segment between (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) internally in ratio m:n has coordinates ((n x1 + m x2)/(m+n), (n y1 + m y2)/(m+n)).
nodes.broader_concept: Coordinate Geometry of Points and Segments

nodes.label: Area of a Triangle in the Coordinate Plane
nodes.title: Given vertices (x1,y1), (x2,y2), (x3,y3), area = 1/2 |x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|.

nodes.label: Circle Equation in Center-Radius Form
nodes.title: (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 represents all points at distance r from center (h,k).

nodes.label: Circle Equation in General Form
nodes.title: x^2 + y^2 + 2g x + 2f y + c = 0 represents a circle with center (-g, -f) and radius r = sqrt(g^2 + f^2 - c), when g^2 + f^2 - c > 0.

nodes.label: Line–Circle Intersection Problems
nodes.title: Solving for points where a line and a circle meet; includes finding zero, one (tangent), or two intersection points.

nodes.label: Circle Centered at the Origin (0,0)
nodes.title: Special case x^2 + y^2 = r^2; simplifies computations in line–circle problems.

nodes.label: Pythagoras’ Theorem in 2D Problem Solving
nodes.title: Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2 to find unknown lengths in two-dimensional right triangles.

nodes.label: Triangle Area Using Trigonometry (A = 1/2 ab sin C)
nodes.title: Compute the area of a triangle from two sides and the included angle using the sine formula.

nodes.label: Sine Rule (Law of Sines) in 2D
nodes.title: Relates sides and angles in any triangle: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.

nodes.label: Cosine Rule (Law of Cosines) in 2D
nodes.title: Relates sides and included angle: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 − 2ab cos C (and cyclic forms).

nodes.label: Sine Function for All Real Angles (Unit Circle Definition)
nodes.title: Define sin θ for any real θ using the y-coordinate on the unit circle.

nodes.label: Cosine Function for All Real Angles (Unit Circle Definition)
nodes.title: Define cos θ for any real θ using the x-coordinate on the unit circle.

nodes.label: Tangent Function Definition
nodes.title: Define tan θ = sin θ / cos θ with domain restrictions where cos θ ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Area of a Sector of a Circle
nodes.title: Compute sector area A = 1/2 r^2 θ for central angle θ in radians.

nodes.label: Arc Length of a Circle
nodes.title: Compute arc length s = r θ for central angle θ in radians.

nodes.label: Exact Trigonometric Ratios in Surd Form
nodes.title: Use exact values like sin 30°, cos 45°, sin 60° expressed with radicals (surds).

nodes.label: 3D Trigonometry Problem Solving
nodes.title: Apply right-triangle trigonometry in three-dimensional contexts (lines of sight, bearings, heights).

nodes.label: Graph of y = sin θ
nodes.title: Plot the sine function showing amplitude, period 2π, and key points.

nodes.label: Graph of y = cos θ
nodes.title: Plot the cosine function showing amplitude, period 2π, and key points.

nodes.label: Graph of y = tan θ
nodes.title: Plot the tangent function showing period π and vertical asymptotes.

nodes.label: Graphing y = a + b sin(cθ)
nodes.title: Transform sine graphs using vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and angular frequency c.

nodes.label: Graphing y = a + b cos(cθ)
nodes.title: Transform cosine graphs using vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and angular frequency c.

nodes.label: Solving sin(nθ) = 0 (General Solutions)
nodes.title: Find all real solutions using periodicity: nθ = kπ, so θ = kπ/n for k ∈ Z.

nodes.label: Solving cos(nθ) = 1/2 (General Solutions)
nodes.title: Find all real solutions using reference angles and periodicity for cosine.

nodes.label: Radian Measure of Angles
nodes.title: Use radians as the natural unit for angle measure and convert between degrees and radians.

nodes.label: Pythagorean Trigonometric Identity
nodes.title: Derive and use sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1 and related identities.

nodes.label: Angle Sum and Difference Identities
nodes.title: Derive and apply sin(A ± B) and cos(A ± B) formulas to solve problems.

nodes.label: Double-Angle Identities
nodes.title: Derive and apply identities for sin 2θ and cos 2θ (and related forms).

nodes.label: Product-to-Sum and Sum-to-Product Identities
nodes.title: Transform products of sines and cosines into sums and vice versa to simplify expressions.

nodes.label: Applying Trigonometric Identities to Simplify and Solve
nodes.title: Use a toolbox of identities (e.g., 1–24 in syllabus) to manipulate expressions and solve equations.

nodes.label: Periodicity and Symmetry of Trigonometric Functions
nodes.title: Use periods (2π for sine/cosine, π for tangent) and even/odd properties in graphs and solutions.

nodes.label: Geometric enlargement (dilation)
nodes.title: A similarity transformation that scales all distances from a fixed centre by a positive scale factor k, preserving shape and angles while multiplying lengths by k.

nodes.label: Scale factor of enlargement (k)
nodes.title: The multiplier applied to all linear dimensions in an enlargement; for this topic k is positive with 0<k<1 (reduction) or k>1 (expansion), and k ∈ Q.

nodes.label: Reductions (0<k<1)
nodes.title: Enlargements with scale factor between 0 and 1 that shrink figures while preserving shape; all lengths are multiplied by k.

nodes.label: Expansions (k>1)
nodes.title: Enlargements with scale factor greater than 1 that increase the size of figures while preserving shape; all lengths are multiplied by k.

nodes.label: Rational scale factors in enlargements (k ∈ Q)
nodes.title: Using rational numbers as scale factors in enlargements for exact ratios in constructions and calculations.

nodes.label: Area scaling under enlargement (k^2 rule)
nodes.title: Under an enlargement with scale factor k, areas are multiplied by k^2.

nodes.label: Similarity properties of enlargements
nodes.title: Enlargements preserve angle measures and shape; corresponding sides are proportional with ratio k and parallelism is preserved.

nodes.label: Construction of an enlargement from a given centre
nodes.title: Procedure: draw rays from the centre through each vertex and locate image points at distance k times the original along each ray.
